status: DESIGN APPENDIX v3 (backlog): rows for milestones M3-M5 and 'post'. Not loaded by the game and not gated by the data test; a row moves into the live file, and under test, when its milestone starts. Rows may reference live ids.
summary: Fish runs, forage, gates, the full almanac with the summer checklist, events and eras beyond the slice.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

region_offsets.rule: Region air = month curve + temp_c; snow depth = month depth x snow_depth_mult. The Oneida Carry and the Oneida country lie under Lake Ontario's lake-effect snow belt: colder and much snowier than Albany (review 1, issue 17).

sap_run.requires_weather: night low below 0 C and day high above 0 C, or thaw
sap_run.balance_intent: About 0.15-0.25 lb of sugar per tap per game day: 30 taps give 5-8 lb a day, a side income and a food and gift store (about 10 gallons of sap a pound).
sap_run.season_total_rule: sugar per tap per game day already uses the flow factor; season totals x0.49

bateau_routes_open.note: the Mohawk and Wood Creek run too low or too high for loaded bateaux outside this window [D]

fish_runs.note: Shad, herring and alewives ran up the Hudson in spring. Cohoes Falls stopped them entering the Mohawk above the falls, so the valley, the fort and the Carry have no shad (review 1, issue 13). Salted shad reaches the valley by trade.
fish_runs.season_total_rule: a whole run's catch is a once-a-year total: multiply by 0.49 (live seasons.json time.season_total_scale)

fish_runs.note: Atlantic salmon ran from Lake Ontario up the Oswego River into Oneida Lake and its creeks in the fall; the Oneida Lake side of the Carry drains to Lake Ontario [H].

The town's harvest observance: a calendar event only; town busy, trade closed that day, visitors by invitation. Name, date and content set with the nation; the post-1799 Longhouse calendar is not imported.
most of the town's men leave for the fall hunt; women, elders and children keep the town, its stores and its fields (N:6, N:7)
last bateaux before the freeze
pork cheap; help wanted
the fall hunters come home with meat and skins for the winter and the spring trade
Midwinter: a calendar event only, never playable; the town is closed to trade and visitors except by invitation. Recorded by the Jesuits as a winter festival; content reviewed with the nation.
neighbours raise a cabin in a day; repay with labour
families shelter in the blockhouse or fort; patrols out
camp fever or smallpox: quarantine, trade stops, prices rise; handled with gravity (conditions.json)

Captives returned under the 1764 treaties at Johnson Hall and Niagara, some unwilling to leave their adoptive families. Bouquet's Muskingum return of the same year belongs to the Ohio node (event.muskingum_1764).
Bouquet's expedition to the Muskingum and the return of captives by Lenape and Shawnee towns

A patentee's Indian deed is challenged as fraudulent: councils, petitions to Johnson, surveys blocked or pushed through. Models the Kayaderosseras patent and the Canajoharie and George Klock disputes (N:32).

Settlers' hogs and cattle break into the corn at Oriska by the Carry, or at Canajoharie, a Mohawk town surrounded by settlers: a real and constant grievance. The senior women ask for restitution; the player can mediate, pay, pen the stock or take a side (standing both ways).
events.v3_note: Moved from the Oneida town: German Flatts lies tens of kilometres from Kanonwalohale (review 1 of v2, minor 9).

events.effects: a weir below another community's fishing place blocks its run; council or magistrate
A scripted, consented kinship or adoption event (npcs.json standing.kinship); never a standing reward.
Johnson's congress at Fort Stanwix: thousands camp at the Carry; demand for provisions and carrying; the new boundary line begins at the Carry itself (era.line_1768_1773).

events.name: Sir William Johnson dies
events.effects: Johnson dies at Johnson Hall on 11 July 1774 during a council with the Six Nations about violence in the Ohio country; Guy Johnson succeeds him as superintendent. Councils pause, colonial authorities' standing with the nations resets partly, and at Canajoharie Molly Brant leaves Johnson Hall and opens her store (N:21, N:41).

events.name: Leave to hunt
events.effects: Oneida fall-hunt parties are on their grounds; a hunter asks leave at their camp or through the interpreter or the post trader (social.ask_leave).

eras.sides: Britain and colonies against New France; nations and communities choose their own alignments
eras.notes: Braddock and Lake George 1755; Fort Bull destroyed 27 March 1756; Oswego falls August 1756; Webb destroys the works on the Carry 31 August 1756; Fort William Henry falls 9 August 1757 and smallpox follows; German Flatts raided November 1757; Fort Stanwix begun 26 August 1758; Fort Frontenac taken, Easton treaty 1758.

eras.sides: the Confederacy joins the British at Niagara (1759); Canadian mission communities make peace at Oswegatchie and Kahnawake (1760)

eras.notes: Amherst cuts gifts and restricts powder; Johnson's and Bouquet's 1761 tariffs at the posts; a Seneca war belt circulates in 1761.

eras.sides: Pontiac's War: many western nations and Genesee Seneca against Britain; Johnson keeps most of the Six Nations out and sends Mohawk and Oneida parties against the Susquehanna Lenape in 1764

eras.notes: The Crown hands Indian trade regulation back to the colonies (1768), where it is weakly enforced; the Fort Stanwix line (November 1768) begins at the Carry; the Frederick Stump murders (January 1768) and settler encroachment raise tension; Shawnee and Lenape reject the cession of their hunting grounds. Potash demand rises (x1.2).

Yellow Creek (April 1774) and Dunmore's War between Virginia and the Shawnee at the Ohio node; the Mingo (Ohio Seneca and Cayuga) under Logan fought, while the Six Nations' council stayed neutral. In the corridor: Johnson's death at Johnson Hall (11 July 1774) during a council about the Ohio violence, and Guy Johnson's succession (event.johnson_death_1774).

military_zone.text: Forts, magazines, sutlers licensed by the commanders, bateau men and Oneida carriers; no tariff board.

tariffs_1761.text: Johnson's and Bouquet's 1761 tariffs posted at the King's posts; gifts cut and powder restricted.

plan_1764.text: The Plan of 1764 as Johnson applied it administratively (it was never enacted by Parliament): trade at posts under commissaries, tariffs and licences, enforced unevenly, until 1768.

colonial_weak.text: Regulation handed back to the colonies in 1768 and weakly enforced: licences nominal, traders go to the towns, prices by bargaining.

aliases.event.green_corn: event.harvest_observance (Haudenosaunee town); Shawnee Green Corn at the Ohio node
